question: Does the consolidated guard coverage retain the intended release authorization and provenance security contracts after removing the older source-grep assertions?
rationale: The code changes only tests, but those tests are the regression boundary for credentialed publish and release-evidence wiring; choosing the minimum durable contract coverage is a maintainer-owned security-policy judgment.

options.title: Accept the consolidated contracts
options.body: Merge after the exact head completes CI and a maintainer confirms the restored release-wiring checks cover the required authorization bindings.

options.title: Preserve additional explicit guards
options.body: Request narrowly identified assertions for any release authorization invariant that maintainers want kept independently visible.

options.title: Pause the refactor
options.body: Keep the existing broader guard suites if maintainers conclude their redundancy is preferable to reduced source-level coverage.

recommendation.title: Accept the consolidated contracts
recommendation.body: Merge after the exact head completes CI and a maintainer confirms the restored release-wiring checks cover the required authorization bindings.

likelyOwner.reason: The assigned author has the most direct, current evidence for the changed guard contracts and can route the final review to the appropriate release-workflow owner.
